q: The continued fraction expansion of a real number α is connected to the Gauss map T: [0,1) → [0,1) by T(x) = {1/x}. The Gauss measure μ(A) = (1/ln 2) ∫_A dx/(1+x) is invariant under T, and the Birkhoff ergodic theorem implies:
opts: All continued fraction partial quotients are equal
The geometric mean of partial quotients converges to the Khinchin constant K ≈ 2.685 for μ-a.e. α
Rational numbers have periodic continued fractions
The Gauss map is conjugate to the doubling map
exp: By the ergodic theorem for the Gauss map with Gauss measure, the geometric mean (a₁a₂⋯aₙ)^{1/n} → K = Π_k (1 + 1/(k(k+2)))^{log₂ k} ≈ 2.685 for a.e. α. This is Khinchin's theorem.
